## Overview:
The PR simplifies `mount()` by registering an inline message handler and changes `unmount()` to only clear the stored socket reference. While the mounted rendering path remains functionally similar, the listener is no longer retained for removal.

The primary risk for specialist review is lifecycle cleanup: after unmounting, the socket may continue invoking the handler, potentially rendering stale views and retaining the `SocketView` instance.

## Strengths:
- Keeps socket assignment and message-to-render behavior straightforward.
- Small, focused diff with no unrelated changes.

resolvedReview.overview:
This PR simplifies `SocketView`'s listener wiring in `src/socket-view.ts`: `mount()` now registers an inline arrow (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`) instead of storing the handler on `this.onMessage`, and `unmount()` replaces the explicit `socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` deregistration with `this.socket = undefined`.

The rendering path itself is unchanged, but the lifecycle cleanup is broken by the refactor: the handler reference is no longer retained, and `unmount()` no longer detaches it. This contradicts the PR description ("preserving existing contracts") and is the one substantive defect in the change.

findings.title: [P1] Remove the "message" listener on unmount instead of only nulling the socket
findings.body: After `mount(socket)` and `unmount()`, the anonymous listener registered at line 14 is never removed — `unmount()` only sets `this.socket = undefined`, and the closure reference was lost by inlining it. On any socket that outlives the view, subsequent `"message"` events still call `this.render(message)` on the unmounted view (stale renders). Because the closure captures `this`, the socket also retains the `SocketView` indefinitely, preventing garbage collection. Repeated mount/unmount cycles on the same socket accumulate listeners, causing duplicate renders and unbounded listener growth. The removed code stored `this.onMessage` precisely so `off("message", this.onMessage)` could deregister it; restore the stored handler (or otherwise keep a reference) and detach it in `unmount()`.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** request_changes

## Overview

This PR simplifies `SocketView`'s listener wiring in `src/socket-view.ts`: `mount()` now registers an inline arrow (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`) instead of storing the handler on `this.onMessage`, and `unmount()` replaces the explicit `socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` deregistration with `this.socket = undefined`.

The rendering path itself is unchanged, but the lifecycle cleanup is broken by the refactor: the handler reference is no longer retained, and `unmount()` no longer detaches it. This contradicts the PR description ("preserving existing contracts") and is the one substantive defect in the change.

## Verification

Verification was not run: no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured (`pr_review_verify` list returned `enabled: false`). Note that baseline execution, if enabled, runs PR code unsandboxed (supervised only at the original POSIX process group; a deliberate `setsid` escape could survive) — an external sandbox/container is recommended for untrusted PRs.

## Findings

### [P1] Remove the "message" listener on unmount instead of only nulling the socket
**Severity:** P1
**Rationale:** After `mount(socket)` and `unmount()`, the anonymous listener registered at line 14 is never removed — `unmount()` only sets `this.socket = undefined`, and the closure reference was lost by inlining it. On any socket that outlives the view, subsequent `"message"` events still call `this.render(message)` on the unmounted view (stale renders). Because the closure captures `this`, the socket also retains the `SocketView` indefinitely, preventing garbage collection. Repeated mount/unmount cycles on the same socket accumulate listeners, causing duplicate renders and unbounded listener growth. The removed code stored `this.onMessage` precisely so `off("message", this.onMessage)` could deregister it; restore the stored handler (or otherwise keep a reference) and detach it in `unmount()`.
**Location:** `src/socket-view.ts:14-18 RIGHT`

## Lane completeness

All requested lanes completed.

## Strengths and notes

- Small, focused diff with no unrelated changes; the message-to-render path itself remains straightforward.
- Correctness: `unmount()` lifecycle contract is broken — see the P1 finding.
- Security: no security issues introduced by this diff.
- Performance: definite listener/view retention leak and listener accumulation on long-lived or reused sockets — same root cause as the P1 finding.
